original_plan: Formal search restricted to PubMed, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, Crossref and arXiv.
change: Added Consensus as a supplementary (non-exhaustive) discovery tool and logged four newly discovered records.
reason: Needed an independent probe for false negatives before subscription and engineering databases become available.
impact_on_review: Confirms the IEEE/ACM/ACL coverage gap empirically; adds four candidates; does not change eligibility criteria. Consensus free tier caps results at 3 per query, so it must be reported as supplementary, never as a primary source of counts.

original_plan: Review described inconsistently as systematic mapping review, systematic review, and living review; reported against PRISMA 2020 only.
change: Fixed review type of record to systematic mapping review; adopted PRISMA-ScR as reporting guideline, PRISMA-S for search reporting, JBI guidance for conduct; dropped the 'living' claim; recorded that PROSPERO does not register mapping reviews and OSF is the registry.
reason: PRISMA 2020 governs systematic reviews of effectiveness and is the wrong guideline for a mapping synthesis; 'living' implies a re-search cadence that was never specified.
impact_on_review: Changes reporting checklist and manuscript methods framing. Does not change research questions, eligibility criteria, or any screening decision already made.

original_plan: Formal search used relevance sorting with a single 100-record page per source.
change: Switched all sources to deterministic date sorting with cursor/offset pagination up to 1000 records; truncation is now reported in the counts CSV; added scripts/test_search_api_contract.py as a live contract test; recorded SHA-256 manifest for the locally cached full-text HTML that is excluded from version control.
reason: Relevance ranking is not stable across time, so the Stage 1 search was not re-runnable, and single-page retrieval silently truncated large result sets; the audit trail also pointed at gitignored files.
impact_on_review: Stage 1 candidate CSVs and counts were produced by the previous non-deterministic code and must be regenerated before final synthesis; existing counts must be preserved in the search log when they are superseded. Does not change eligibility criteria.
